corrected_content.problem: Find $f(x, y, z)$ such that $\mathrm{∇}f(x,y,z)=\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)$, where $\mathbf{F}(x,y,z)=2xy\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{i}+({x}^{2}+2z)\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{j}+2y\hspace{0.167em}\mathbf{k}$.
corrected_content.worked_solution: Integrate $f_x=2xy$ with respect to $x$: $f=x^2y+g(y,z)$. Matching $f_y=x^2+2z$ gives $g_y=2z$, so $g=2yz+h(z)$. Finally $f_z=2y+h'(z)=2y$, hence $h$ is constant. Therefore $$f=x^2y+2yz+C.$$ Its three partial derivatives reproduce all components of $F$.

choices.value: f(x, y, z) = x^{2}yz + yz^{2} + C
f(x, y, z) = x^{2}y + yz + Cxz
